---
title: "Scenarios: car speeds and traffic stress"
description: >
  Change the car speed of streets, by way or by area, and the level of
  traffic stress cyclists meet, for one routing call.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("setup.R")
```

Every routing function takes three arguments that change the street network
for that call only: `new_carspeeds` (car speeds by 'OpenStreetMap' way, or
by area), `carspeed_scale` (a factor for every other street) and `new_lts`
(levels of traffic stress for cyclists, by way or by line). The network
itself does not change. This page uses the Porto Alegre sample of r5r 2.5.0
and the scenario tables that come with it.

```{r data, message = FALSE}
library(peabiru)
poa <- poa_sample(c("poa_osm.pbf", "poa_hexgrid.csv", "poa_osm_congestion.csv",
                    "poa_poly_congestion.rds", "poa_osm_lts.csv", "poa_ls_lts.rds"))
poa_network <- build_network(poa, n_threads = 2)
hexes <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_hexgrid.csv"))
pts <- hexes[seq(1, nrow(hexes), by = 25), ]

car <- function(...) {
  travel_time_matrix(poa_network, pts, pts, mode = "CAR", n_threads = 2, ...)
}
base <- car()
mean(base$travel_time_p50)
```

## Car speeds by way

A data frame with `osm_id`, `max_speed` and `speed_type` gives, for each
way, a factor of its car speed (`"scale"`) or a new speed (`"km/h"`); a
speed of 0 closes the way to cars.

```{r ways}
congestion <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_osm_congestion.csv"))
head(congestion)
slow <- car(new_carspeeds = congestion)
mean(slow$travel_time_p50)
```

`carspeed_scale` multiplies the car speed of every street the table leaves
out (all of them without a table):

```{r scale}
rush_hour <- car(carspeed_scale = 0.7)
mean(rush_hour$travel_time_p50)
```

Car speeds are kept, as in R5, as 16-bit centimetres per second, so a
factor or a speed that would bring a speed to 0 or less, or beyond that
range, is an error rather than a wrapped-around speed.

## Car speeds by area

An `sf` data frame of polygons with `poly_id`, `scale` and `priority` gives
each street the factor of the polygon it meets with the highest priority
(ties: the one it overlaps most).

```{r polygons, eval = requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
areas <- readRDS(file.path(poa, "poa_poly_congestion.rds"))
areas
by_area <- car(new_carspeeds = areas)
mean(by_area$travel_time_p50)
```

## Traffic stress

`new_lts` changes the level of traffic stress (1 to 4) cyclists meet, by
way (`osm_id`, `lts`) or along lines (an `sf` of `LINESTRING`s with
`line_id`, `lts` and `priority`, each street taking the level of the
nearest line). A cyclist rides only on streets up to `max_lts` and walks
the bicycle elsewhere:

```{r lts}
lts <- read.csv(file.path(poa, "poa_osm_lts.csv"))
head(lts)
bike <- function(...) {
  travel_time_matrix(poa_network, pts, pts, mode = "BICYCLE", max_lts = 2,
                     n_threads = 2, ...)
}
c(base = mean(bike()$travel_time_p50),
  scenario = mean(bike(new_lts = lts)$travel_time_p50))
```

A scenario changes the street search from the origins (the trip without
public transport, and access to it by bicycle or car) but not the egress
from the stops, and, on a network with an elevation raster, the call runs
without slope costs, with a warning (see [Elevation](elevation.html)).
